account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: market business, lunch, accounts, and tea with my neighbour. The baker reported eighty fresh loaves and asked for reliable wheat from the mill. I asked the secretary to obtain quantities, prices, and delivery terms ahead of tomorrow's mill inspection. Accounts were unusually thin: neither I nor the secretary had a ledger, invoices, or payment requests to review. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, and I authorized no payments. That is an administrative gap, not evidence of wrongdoing.

A few things have caught my attention. At the market I heard freight ask the baker to discuss a warehouse order privately at the bakery later. I do not know what the order contains or why privacy was wanted; it could simply be ordinary business. Builder specifically requested a brief great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at exactly eighteen hundred, and asked the secretary to bring me into the hall. Builder said the purpose was checking whether new lanterns give even lighting, with no urgent problem. The precise timing is memorable, but I have seen no evidence of another purpose.

My neighbour now says the docks have been peaceful and nothing unusual has been noticed. They report the baker explained some lights as an oven glowing for fresh bread. I did not personally investigate those lights. They also mentioned vague bridge and port rumours but had no concrete information, so I cannot treat those as established events or connect them to the warehouse order or lighting inspection.

I still have a feeling that town business may be happening without me, but nothing I have learned establishes a secret scheme. The known activities could all concern bread supply, ordinary freight, and hall maintenance. I should return for my 16:30 office appointment and keep tomorrow's recorded appointments, including the eighteen hundred inspection.
